title: Decode hedge orchestrator: bandit model-selection, kernel-fit scoring, and failsafe playbook
creator: Maya Chen
description: Background: We need a lightweight runtime component (the "hedge orchestrator") that can send a small set of concurrent speculative decode attempts to alternate model/kernel combos, score their early outputs with a fast bandit-style scorer, and commit the cheapest acceptable output. Problem: current runtime only does single-path decode or coarse fallback; we want safer optimism: try faster/cheaper paths but ensure strict acceptance thresholds and deterministic failsafe fallbacks to avoid user-visible regressions or SLA violations. Scope: design runtime arbitration, define acceptance metrics, kernel-fit scoring heuristics, safe rollback/fallback policies, telemetry/alerts, and an incremental rollout plan. Out of scope: full multi-region traffic steering and new model compression tools.
acceptance_criteria: Hedge orchestrator commits a speculative output only when acceptance_score >= 0.92 (configurable) and model-compatibility check passes
When the first candidate fails acceptance, orchestrator falls back to baseline model within latency SLO 99th percentile + 15ms
End-to-end p50 latency on hedge path reduction >= 18% for the selected workload compared to baseline, without increasing failure rate > 0.2%
Telemetry for all hedged requests is emitted (candidate_scores, kernel_id, chosen_candidate, fallback_reason) and visible in runtime dashboards
Automated canary that progressively enables hedge routing for 1%, 10%, 50% traffic with health gates succeeds before broader rollout
design_notes: Architecture: lightweight arbiter sits alongside existing prefill/decode scheduler. On incoming request, arbiter may launch a prefilling probe to 1..N alternative model/kernel candidates (N default=2) using limited KV-cache prefill and a short decode horizon (first 8 tokens).

Scoring: bandit-style fast scorer uses: token-level logprob delta vs baseline, alignment with structured-output schema (if present), and kernel-fit penalty derived from recent kernel latency variance. Score is normalized to [0,1].
Kernel-fit heuristic: prefer kernels that historically meet token-latency SLO for the request's sequence-length bucket; compute a kernel_affinity = exp(-latency_stddev / median_latency).

Acceptance envelope: different thresholds per customer tier and per route; default acceptance_score threshold=0.92 but can be tightened for high-security routes. Acceptance requires pass on syntactic checks (balanced JSON, no hallucination markers) for structured tasks.

Fallback policy matrix: 1) soft-fail: if candidate marginally below threshold, allow baseline decode to run in parallel and choose later winner; 2) hard-fail: if candidate fails clear rejection checks, cancel speculative paths and return baseline; 3) degraded-mode: if kernels fail catastrophically, route to smaller model variant in dedicated pool with graceful reductions in max_tokens.
Resource controls: speculative attempts must be budgeted in the scheduler. Each customer has a speculative token budget per minute; defaults set to 5% of token quota to limit cost regressions.
Traceability: every decision emits trace spans and a compact decision record (candidate_ids, score_vector, kernel_ids, reason). These are stored in the runtime event stream for 30 days by default.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (lab): unit + integration tests against synthetic workloads; fuzz acceptance metrics with adversarial prompts
Phase 1 (canary 1%): enable hedge orchestrator for internal services and low-risk customers; monitor acceptance_rate, revert_ratio, 99th latency delta; run for 72h
Phase 2 (scale 10%): expand to non-critical public routes with stricter health gates; enable kernel_fit telemetry sampling at 100% for hedged requests
Phase 3 (gradual): 50% -> 100% with per-route opt-outs; enable cost-control automation to throttle speculation when monthly token spend delta > 8%
Emergency rollback: config flag to globally disable hedging; automated rollback if critical SLA breaches detected
test_plan: Unit tests: scorer math, kernel_affinity calculations, decision branches
Integration: end-to-end prefill+hedge flows with mocked kernels and KV caches
Perf: realistic load tests on staging GPUs measuring p50/p95/p99 for hedged vs baseline, cost delta per-token
Chaos: kill speculative kernel processes mid-prefill to validate fallback and idempotency
A/B evals: quality evaluations using held-out prompt set to validate no regression in BLEU/ROUGE/semantic-similarity metrics
telemetry_requirements: Emit candidate_score vector and chosen_candidate as structured logs for every hedged request
Tag traces with kernel_id, model_variant, prefill_length, and acceptance_reason
Dashboard: per-route acceptance_rate, commit_latency, fallback_reasons, cost_delta, and per-kernel success rate
Alerting: fire when fallback_rate > 0.5% for 15m or when acceptance_rate drops > 5 percentage points vs baseline
